Running Linux Mint as a dual-boot beside Win 10. I like Mint a lot, I want to like it more but it's limiting.

Pros: Worked right out of the box, the Software Manager is GREAT and no more downloading and installing updates off websites like a chump (repos FTW!), snappy interface with tons of customization, lots of free software, playing around in the terminal makes me feel like a bad-ass hacker

Cons: limited support (no Adobe products, limited driver support), a lot of deep trust in reading articles and copy-pasting stuff into the terminal to install or configure things (I don't like not knowing what I'm doing at that access level on my OS), finding it really difficult to do seemingly simple things (like changing my monitor refresh rate from 60 to 75hz involved editing system config files with a text editor - very over complicated for a simple thing), a lot of games are N/A and even more run like shit if they run at all.

Linux Mint is a very competent OS. I enjoy using it for web browsing, listening to music, using it with KODI. The games that are WELL supported run very well (just finished SOMA) - but, if you're not open to spending a lot of time reading posts on forums or not spending time tinkering with it a lot it just isn't the OS for you.... that, and I have close to 30 years of working in windows so it's just hard to make the plunge into the unfamiliar.
